answer.answer: Straylight is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth. The 2026-07-26 current-status note controls because it explicitly supersedes the older green checkpoint. Production-scale retrieval timeouts, shared-transaction rollback across retrieval lanes, and full-manifest copying on normal writes invalidate the earlier owner-alpha recommendation. The approved direction is a Markdown-first, changed-file-only architecture with rebuildable derived data and exact-reference checkpoints.

claims.value: `Projects/Straylight current status.md`, updated 2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00, is authoritative because it explicitly supersedes `Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md`. The older note, recorded 2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00, is historical evidence: its passing retrieval test corpus, healthy `/ready` configuration, and immediate owner-alpha proposal predate the production-sized timeout and full-manifest-copy findings and must not override the newer note.

Connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, but broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Retrieval lanes also share one transaction, so a later lane failure can discard an earlier lane’s successful result. Consequently, current retrieval is not dependable for owner use at 10x corpus growth.

The owner corpus currently has about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens, and every normal write copies a full corpus membership manifest. This production-scale write amplification is one reason the current architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

The approved proposal is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth, version only changed files, and make indexes and derived views rebuildable. Checkpoints should reference exact path, version, and hash values plus changes since a workspace generation, while preserving coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets. This is the approved direction, not yet a verified completed implementation.
